issues.existing: A dark, near-monochrome depiction of a crowned figure seated on an ornate throne at the edge of a stone causeway, with a fortress on a crag in the distance.
issues.observed: The figure's head is entirely in shadow; no crown or headpiece is resolvable, and it may equally read as a hood or loose dark hair.
issues.evidence: At the head there is only an unbroken dark mass with no points, band or highlight; the model itself lists 'whether the figure wears a crown or headpiece' as uncertain yet the scene line asserts it flatly.

issues.existing: flight of steps rising to a small arched gate
issues.observed: A flight of steps is visible in the middle distance on the road, but no arched gate or arched structure can be resolved at its top.
issues.evidence: The steps fade into unmodulated black before any opening appears; the only architecture I can separate is the fortress silhouette much further up the crag.

replace.with: a dark-robed figure, head bowed and in shadow, seated on an ornate throne

replace.find: flight of steps rising to a small arched gate
replace.with: flight of steps rising along the road toward the fortress

issues.existing: torn paper or parchment sheet split by the blade
issues.observed: An open book lying face-up on the slab — two pale facing pages tented up from a central gutter, with a visible page-block thickness at the front edge — not a single flat sheet, and not torn.
issues.evidence: The pale form reads as two planes meeting in a V at the centre where the blade tip sits, and the front edge of the object shows the stepped thickness of a stack of pages; there is no tear line anywhere apart from the blade itself.

issues.existing: the intact sheet of paper against its clean tear
issues.observed: Same error carried forward: the object is an open book, and no tear is visible in it.
issues.evidence: The only thing interrupting the pages is the blade tip resting in the central gutter.

issues.existing: the woman stands to the left of the panel, her hands at its upper edge
issues.observed: She is kneeling/crouching low behind the panel, not standing; her legs are bent under her and her torso leans forward over the frame.
issues.evidence: A bent pale-clad knee and lower leg are clearly visible at the lower left beneath her green cloak, and her shoulders sit barely above the frame's top rail — a standing figure could not be that low relative to a panel whose base rests on the ground.

issues.existing: large weathered wooden panel or board
issues.observed: A square wooden frame holding stretched coarse woven cloth, i.e. an embroidery/tapestry frame — the working surface is fabric, not wood.
issues.evidence: The whole inner face shows a visible warp-and-weft weave running to the frame's edges, and the heart patch and blades are stitched through it; the wood is only the four surrounding bars.

issues.existing: the sword stands vertically at the centre, its point rising above the figure's head
issues.observed: The blade is vertical but POINT-DOWN: its tip is driven into the top of the stone altar. What rises above the figure's head is the crossguard, grip and pommel.
issues.evidence: The horizontal quillons sit high at the top of the frame with a short grip and small finial above them, and the bright blade runs downward from there through the figure's hand into the altar top — where a large crack splits the block's front face directly in line with the tip.

issues.existing: the boat occupies the lower centre, its bow toward the viewer
issues.observed: The boat is seen from ASTERN — the stern, with its carved decorative transom panel, faces the viewer; the bow points away toward the lit horizon.
issues.evidence: The near end is the wide, rounded end carrying a carved panel and the boat's interior recedes away from it, narrowing to a point at the far end; both figures face away from the viewer toward that far end and the horizon glow.

issues.existing: Two cloaked figures sit in a wooden rowboat on dark water, one rowing
issues.observed: Only one figure is seated; the other is standing upright, working the oar/pole with both hands.
issues.evidence: The rear figure's full torso, shoulders and head rise well above the seated figure's, with the cloak hanging in vertical folds to the boat's floor — the model's own keyObjects line already says 'held by the standing figure'.
